units.title: Unit 55 — Agreeing and disagreeing
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 114–115 (PDF pages 118–119).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
learningObjectives: Distinguish acknowledging or understanding another person’s view from agreeing with it.
Express full, partial and principled disagreement with appropriate adverbs and politeness.
Describe direct confrontations, unresolved conflicts and compromise using natural noun collocations.
Use agreement and dispute expressions accurately in meetings, negotiation and discussion.

items.pt: concordar com uma ideia; apoiar uma proposta
items.example: I cannot go along with an idea that would exclude part-time employees.
items.note: Go along with means accept or support an idea, sometimes reluctantly.

items.pt: concordar com um ponto de vista
items.example: Several committee members go along with the view that the rules need revising.
items.note: View means an opinion or position on a question; go along with signals agreement.

items.pt: estar de acordo; concordar
items.example: The engineers seem to be in agreement about the safest solution.
items.note: A relatively formal way to express agreement, often followed by about, on or over.

items.pt: estar em pleno acordo; concordar completamente
items.example: We appear to be in complete agreement on the project priorities.
items.note: Complete makes the level of agreement emphatic.

items.pt: tender a concordar
items.example: I tend to agree with the proposal, although I still have a few concerns.
items.note: Tend to softens a statement and avoids expressing absolute certainty.

items.pt: tender a discordar
items.example: I tend to disagree with the assumption that longer meetings produce better decisions.
items.note: A diplomatic alternative to a categorical expression of disagreement.

items.pt: partilhar uma opinião; ter uma opinião em comum
items.example: We share an opinion about the importance of independent testing.
items.note: Share an opinion means hold the same view; it does not mean merely state an opinion.

items.pt: compartilhar um ponto de vista
items.example: The researchers share a view on the need for more reliable data.
items.note: View and opinion are close in this context, but they are not interchangeable in every expression.

items.pt: compreender seu ponto de vista; reconhecer seu argumento
items.example: I appreciate your point of view, but the deadline cannot be extended.
items.note: Appreciate can show respectful understanding without agreeing with someone.

items.pt: entender seu ponto; compreender seu raciocínio
items.example: I see your point, yet I still think a second test is necessary.
items.note: See someone’s point expresses understanding, not necessarily agreement.

items.pt: entrar em uma discussão; envolver-se em uma discussão
items.example: I do not want to enter into an argument over such a minor mistake.
items.note: This usually means become involved in a dispute, not simply start a neutral conversation.

items.pt: há divergências; existem diferenças de opinião
items.example: Differences exist between the two departments over the new staffing plan.
items.note: Differences can refer to disagreements between people or groups.

items.pt: surgem divergências; aparecem desentendimentos
items.example: Differences arise when teams interpret the same requirements differently.
items.note: Arise means come into existence; exist describes a continuing state.

items.pt: chegar a um acordo por meio de concessões
items.example: After a difficult discussion, both sides managed to come to a compromise.
items.note: A compromise normally involves each side giving up something it wanted.

items.pt: chegar a um meio-termo; alcançar um acordo
items.example: The partners hope to reach a compromise before Friday.
items.note: Reach a compromise has the same core meaning as come to a compromise.

items.pt: resolver uma disputa; solucionar um conflito
items.example: The independent mediator helped settle a dispute about overtime payments.
items.note: Settle means resolve a disagreement; the conflict can involve work, money or other issues.

items.pt: resolver nossas divergências; acertar nossas diferenças
items.example: We should settle our differences before we begin the joint project.
items.note: Common with possessive determiners; it emphasises reconciliation between people.

items.pt: concordar em discordar
items.example: We cannot agree on the design, so perhaps we should agree to differ.
items.note: The parties accept that they hold different opinions without continuing the dispute.

items.pt: concordar inteiramente; concordar plenamente
items.example: I entirely agree that the procedure should be documented.
items.note: Entirely indicates full agreement, especially in careful or formal discussion.

items.pt: concordar de todo o coração; concordar sem reservas
items.example: I wholeheartedly agree with the decision to improve accessibility.
items.note: Wholeheartedly conveys enthusiastic and sincere agreement.

items.pt: concordar em parte; concordar parcialmente
items.example: I partly agree with your assessment, but it overlooks the maintenance costs.
items.note: Partly limits the scope of agreement and invites qualification.

items.pt: concordar até certo ponto
items.example: I agree up to a point, but the proposed budget is still unrealistic.
items.note: A useful expression for partial agreement followed by a reservation.

items.pt: discordar fundamentalmente; discordar em pontos essenciais
items.example: I fundamentally disagree with the suggestion that safety checks are optional.
items.note: Fundamentally signals disagreement on a basic principle, not a small detail.

items.pt: discordar totalmente
items.example: The two reviewers totally disagree about the quality of the report.
items.note: Totally stresses complete disagreement and can sound quite direct.

items.pt: discordar veementemente; discordar fortemente
items.example: I strongly disagree with the decision to remove the independent review.
items.note: Strongly intensifies disagreement without necessarily suggesting personal hostility.

items.pt: um confronto direto; um embate frontal
items.example: The public hearing ended in a head-on clash between the two campaign groups.
items.note: A head-on clash is a direct confrontation between opposing positions; the image suggests a collision.

items.pt: uma disputa acirrada; um conflito amargo
items.example: A bitter dispute over wages lasted for several months.
items.note: Bitter suggests intense resentment or hostility rather than a disagreement over taste.

items.pt: uma discussão acalorada
items.example: A heated argument broke out over the proposed changes to the timetable.
items.note: Heated indicates strong emotion or anger; it is figurative.

items.pt: uma divergência fundamental; um desacordo de princípio
items.example: There is a fundamental disagreement about who should approve the results.
items.note: Fundamental describes a disagreement involving essential principles or assumptions.

items.pt: chegar a um acordo unânime
items.example: After reviewing the evidence, the panel managed to reach a unanimous agreement.
items.note: Unanimous means every relevant member agrees; it does not mean merely a large majority.

items.pt: a controvérsia continua; a polêmica persiste
items.example: Controversy continues over whether the historic building should be replaced.
items.note: A neutral way to say an issue is still disputed.

items.pt: a polêmica se intensifica; a controvérsia segue acirrada
items.example: Controversy rages over the future of the coastal development.
items.note: Rages is vivid language suggesting an intense or prolonged public argument.

items.pt: um conflito de opiniões; divergência de pontos de vista
items.example: A conflict of opinion within the board delayed the appointment.
items.note: A formal way to describe competing views within a group.

items.pt: opiniões conflitantes; pontos de vista divergentes
items.example: The committee received conflicting opinions from independent experts.
items.note: Conflicting emphasises that the views are incompatible; it is a valid exercise-derived alternative.

items.pt: divergências de opinião
items.example: Differences of opinion are normal in a multidisciplinary team.
items.note: A standard way to refer to disagreements without implying personal hostility.

B · Verb and adverb collocations: degrees of agreement and disagreement
C · Adjective and noun collocations for disputes and strong disagreements
D · Further collocations for agreeing and disagreeing

units.title: Unit 56 — Talking about beliefs and opinions
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 116–117 (PDF pages 120–121).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Functions · talking about beliefs and opinions
learningObjectives: Express strongly held, popular and tentative beliefs using natural word combinations.
Use more formal collocations to question evidence, identify assumptions and state considered opinions.
Describe uncertainty, divided opinions and misgivings without overstating certainty.
Avoid common learner errors involving hope and wish, think and consider, and modifiers of opinions.

items.pt: acreditar firmemente; estar firmemente convencido
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: I firmly believe that the new training programme will improve safety.
items.note: Firmly emphasises strong conviction; a that-clause can state what is believed.

items.pt: compartilhar sua opinião; concordar com seu ponto de vista
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: I share your opinion on the need for better public transport.
items.note: Means hold the same view as the person addressed; not simply exchange opinions.

items.word: a great believer in practical training
items.pt: um grande defensor da formação prática; alguém que acredita muito no treinamento prático
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: My supervisor is a great believer in practical training.
items.note: Be a great believer in something means strongly support its value or effectiveness.

items.pt: crença popular; opinião difundida
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: Popular belief does not always reflect the available scientific evidence.
items.note: Popular means widely held rather than necessarily correct or well liked.

items.pt: ao contrário do que muitos acreditam
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: Contrary to popular belief, a larger battery does not always mean a heavier device.
items.note: Used to introduce information that challenges a widely held assumption.

items.pt: ter motivos para acreditar
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: We have reason to believe that the package was delivered to the wrong address.
items.note: Signals a basis for a belief, while stopping short of absolute proof.

items.pt: diametralmente opostos; com posições totalmente diferentes
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: The two candidates are poles apart on environmental policy.
items.note: An informal figurative expression for extremely different opinions or attitudes.

items.pt: uma questão de opinião
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: Whether the design is attractive is a matter of opinion.
items.note: Used when there is no single objectively established answer.

items.pt: uma divergência de opinião
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: We had a difference of opinion about which supplier to choose.
items.note: A polite, relatively neutral way to acknowledge disagreement.

items.pt: uma leve suspeita; uma desconfiança
items.section: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions
items.example: I have a sneaking suspicion that the test was run with the wrong settings.
items.note: Sneaking suggests a private or tentative suspicion that has gradually developed.

items.pt: fazer suposições; presumir sem evidências suficientes
items.example: We should not make assumptions about the cause before checking the logs.
items.note: An assumption is treated as true without adequate evidence; make is the natural verb.

items.pt: uma convicção inabalável
items.example: She has an unshakeable belief in the importance of equal opportunities.
items.note: Unshakeable means extremely firm and resistant to challenge.

items.pt: um conjunto de crenças; um sistema de convicções
items.example: His approach reflects a set of beliefs he developed over many years.
items.note: Set groups related beliefs rather than referring to one isolated opinion.

items.pt: influenciar seu julgamento; distorcer sua avaliação
items.example: Personal disappointment can colour your judgement of a colleague.
items.note: Colour means influence an assessment, often making it less objective; British spelling is colour.

items.pt: levar-nos a concluir
items.example: These repeated measurements lead us to conclude that the device is stable.
items.note: Lead someone to conclude introduces a conclusion inferred from evidence.

items.pt: atribuir importância a; dar importância a
items.example: Good researchers attach importance to documenting unexpected results.
items.note: Importance is uncountable; the construction is attach importance to something.

items.pt: atribuir importância excessiva a
items.example: It is risky to attach too much importance to one isolated result.
items.note: Too much suggests that something is being treated as more significant than it deserves.

items.pt: confiar no seu discernimento; confiar em sua avaliação
items.example: In an emergency, you should trust your judgement while following the safety procedure.
items.note: Judgement is the British spelling; trust means rely on someone’s ability to decide well.

items.pt: colocar em dúvida; lançar dúvidas sobre
items.example: The inconsistent results cast doubt on the original conclusion.
items.note: A relatively formal expression meaning raise questions about reliability or truth.

items.pt: as opiniões estão divididas
items.example: Opinions are divided on whether the city should extend the cycle lanes.
items.note: A passive construction indicating that people hold opposing views.

items.pt: uma opinião ponderada; uma avaliação refletida
items.example: After reading the evidence, I formed a considered opinion on the proposal.
items.note: Considered means formed after careful thought, not merely taken into account.

items.pt: ter sérias reservas; ter grandes preocupações
items.example: I have serious misgivings about releasing the software without further tests.
items.note: Misgivings are doubts or worries about whether a course of action is wise.

items.pt: ter dúvidas; ter incertezas
items.example: I have doubts about the accuracy of the initial estimate.
items.note: Often followed by a noun or -ing form describing what is uncertain.

items.pt: espero que você possa vir
items.example: I hope you can come to the exhibition on Saturday.
items.note: Use hope to express a desired possible future event, not wish in this construction.

items.pt: perder as esperanças; desistir de ter esperança
items.example: Despite the delay, the families refused to give up hope.
items.note: Normally no definite article before hope in this expression.

items.pt: pensar bastante sobre; refletir cuidadosamente a respeito de
items.example: We need to think hard about the risks before changing the design.
items.note: Hard modifies think; consider hard is not the natural equivalent.

items.pt: considerar o problema cuidadosamente; analisar a questão com atenção
items.example: We should consider the problem carefully before deciding on a solution.
items.note: Consider takes the object directly and combines naturally with carefully, not hard.

items.word: wish they would leave me alone
items.pt: queria que eles me deixassem em paz
items.example: Sometimes I wish they would leave me alone while I work.
items.note: Wish plus would can express frustration about someone else’s behaviour.

items.word: hold the view that prevention matters
items.pt: sustentar a opinião de que a prevenção é importante
items.example: Many doctors hold the view that prevention matters more than treatment alone.
items.note: Hold the view that introduces a belief in fairly formal discussion; meaning is not used for opinion.

items.word: hold the opinion that costs will rise
items.pt: ter a opinião de que os custos aumentarão
items.example: Some economists hold the opinion that costs will rise under the proposed policy.
items.note: An alternative to hold the view that, generally followed by a clause.

items.pt: opiniões fortes; convicções firmes
items.example: She has strong opinions on the use of artificial intelligence in schools.
items.note: Strong is the normal modifier here, rather than heavy or big.

items.pt: ter uma opinião diferente
items.example: My colleague may have a different opinion about the best approach.
items.note: Opinion is the correct noun for an individual viewpoint; not meaning in this sense.

sectionsChecked: A · Speaking about beliefs and opinions: conviction, suspicion and differences
B · More formal ways of discussing beliefs and research conclusions
C · Common learner-error contrasts: hope/wish, think/consider and strong opinions
